You can now get an IDNYC card  **without an appointment**  at certain locations. **Walk-ins** are welcome on a  **first-come, first-served**  basis at these locations on these days:

All other locations still require an appointment. New appointments are available every **Friday** for the following week (**Monday to Friday**).

Appointments are released each week on Friday, for the following Monday through Friday. To schedule an appointment, [click here](https://a069-idnyconlineportal.nyc.gov/IOPWeb/#/appointment/) or call **311** to make an appointment. Do not book more than one appointment per person. If you cannot make it to your scheduled appointment, please cancel, and reschedule for a later date or time.

Please arrive on time for your appointment.

Before your visit, please check which identity and residency documents you need to bring. You can use the IDNYC [Document Calculator](https://www.nyc.gov/site/idnyc/card/documentation.page) to find out what documents are required.

Applicants with appointments are given a 15-minute grace period on their appointment time, based on the Enrollment Center capacity.

# WIC Program

#### WIC Program

Keeping parents and their babies healthy is the goal of the Women, Infants and Children (WIC) program. WIC is a federally funded, state-run program that focuses on the nutritional well-being of pregnant people and new parents, as well as their children up to age five.

#### Who is Eligible?

Pregnant, breastfeeding and non-breastfeeding parents, infants, and children up to five years old may be eligible for the WIC program. In addition, fathers or other legal guardians may also be eligible to receive WIC benefits for their infants and children up to age five. Our friendly, dedicated staff will help determine whether you qualify for WIC and help you through the application process.

To qualify for WIC you must:

* Be a resident of New York State (though you don’t have to be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident)
* Meet certain income requirements

For more information about the WIC program, visit [www.health.ny.gov/prevention/nutrition/wic/](https://www.health.ny.gov/prevention/nutrition/wic/)

[To submit your application click here](#WICapplication)

#### How WIC Helps You

Once you are enrolled in our WIC program you will meet with one of our WIC nutritionists, who will counsel you about how to stay healthier before and after pregnancy. WIC nutritionists teach participants that food choices, lifestyle, overall health, and behavior affect pregnancy and child development. Our nutritionists will also advise you on creative ways to encourage children to eat more fruits and vegetables to help them get a better start in life.

WIC parents and their kids save money on food when they take advantage of this free program, part of which includes monthly WIC benefits to be used specifically on nutritionally healthy food options. The money can be used at regular grocery stores to purchase food for your family. Our staff will discuss the food package, details about which foods can be purchased with the WIC check, and how to get the most out of your monthly allowance.

The WIC program also provides:

* Breastfeeding classes
* Peer Support and Counseling
* Classes on feeding your children

In addition to this nutritional support, WIC staff is a great referral source for medical and other health care needs for you and your family.

# Family Welcome Centers (FWCs)

FWCs support families enrolling in NYC Public Schools with specific enrollment needs. Parents and guardians can schedule a virtual or in-person appointment at any location to get help with school enrollment. FWCs are open Monday - Thursday from 8am - 5pm, and Friday from 8am - 3pm.

![Illustration of dad and daughter at a desk talking to enrollment](https://pwsblobprd.schools.nyc/prd-pws/images/default-source/default-album/enrollment/enrollment-help/fwc-family-chat.svg?sfvrsn=99b1aed6_8)

## Services

Family Welcome Centers provide specific services. If your child has a zoned school or received an offer from a school through the admissions process, you need to contact that school directly for enrollment help. Family Welcome Centers can offer specific enrollment services which are listed below.

Get help enrolling a student in a NYC public school, whether new, returning, or switching from a charter or private school, and submit required documents online.

Get help transferring a student from one NYC public school to another. This includes travel hardship transfers for high school students.

Get assistance with exploring schools, applying, and checking waitlist status in MySchools.

## Book an Appointment

Before visiting, please review the information below.

You will need to provide ID and enrollment documentation during your meeting. Review the list of accepted documents on our Registration Checklist. Be prepared to provide this information electronically for virtual appointments.

[Enrollment Forms](/enrollment/enrollment-help/enrollment-forms)

Our office cannot make changes to the application or waitlist process. If you would like to explore other school options, you must add your child to the waitlists of other desired schools through your MySchools account.

[MySchools](https://www.myschools.nyc/)

New and returning elementary or middle school students do not need to visit our office. You can find your zoned school using our Find a School tool, and enroll directly at the school.

[Find a School](https://schoolsearch.schools.nyc/)

If you cannot find an appointment that works for you, please call 718-935-2828 for assistance in finding a date and time that work for you.

# Please Note

# New Life Food Pantry: Hot Meals & Grocery Delivery Program

Our Food Pantry serves the Elmhurst and Corona community’s homeless and low-income residents with hot meals-to-go and weekly deliveries of non-perishable food and fresh produce to those that continue to be food insecure. Nearly two in three children in Elmhurst and Corona live in households in or near poverty and wage earners typically work disproportionately in lower-wage professions mainly in construction and hospitality-related sectors. 62% of Elmhurst and Corona residents are rent burdened, a higher rate than residents citywide. Rent burdened households pay more than 30% of their income for housing and may have difficulty affording food, clothing, transportation and health care. Since the pandemic, many are still unemployed or are working reduced hours.

Tuesdays, 5 pm - 7 pm  /  Saturdays, 10 am - 12 pm

### Services

We’re more than just a health center—we’re your partner in wellness. In addition to high quality primary care services for the entire family, we provide specialty care like mental health services, gynecology, family planning, on-site mammography screening, breast imaging, optometry, and nutrition support. Our mission is to help you achieve the best health outcomes possible, offering the highest level of care and health education so you can continue working toward your health goals beyond your visits with us.

At Urban Health Plan, we understand that your health is shaped by more than just medical care. That’s why we offer social services and referrals to help you overcome barriers like food insecurity, housing challenges, and unemployment. We’re here to support you in every aspect of your health journey.

No insurance? No worries! Our bilingual team is here to assist, regardless of your insurance status. We can also help determine your eligibility for insurance benefits and guide you through the enrollment process.

We’re open six days a week with flexible hours to fit your busy schedule. Whether you want to give us a call or walk in, we are here to make healthcare convenient and accessible for you and your family. We can’t wait to welcome you!

## About This Location

Welcome to Corona Library! Visit your local QPL branch for books, movies, music, free Wi-Fi, free computer workstations, classes, programs, and so much more.

No matter who you are, where you’re from, or where you want to go, at Queens Public Library, we speak your language.

Remote Printing is available at this QPL location. Visit <https://queenslib.org/qplprint> to learn more.

This QPL location has Extended Wi-Fi. If you’re within 450 feet of this branch, you can connect automatically to our wireless network, QPL\_Wi-Fi, whether we are open or closed, no sign-in required!
